nd9c2bd464ae.s: Which dynasty succeeded the Mamluks on the throne of Delhi in 1290?
nd9c2bd464ae.x: The Mamluk dynasty (1206–1290) was followed by the Khaljis (1290–1320), then the Tughlaqs, Sayyids and Lodis.

n48109b2f182.s: In which year did Alauddin Khalji conquer Malwa?
n48109b2f182.x: Malwa fell in 1305, after Gujarat (1299), Ranthambhor (1301) and Chittor (1303).

n27447158f87.s: Alauddin Khalji revived the harsh, centralised rule of which earlier Sultan, though without depending on religious sanction?
n27447158f87.x: Alauddin revived Balban's harsh, centralised rule but, unlike Balban, did not depend on religious sanction.

n1c6163ff8f0.s: Which Sultan abolished Alauddin Khalji's price controls and restored confiscated lands after ascending the throne?
n1c6163ff8f0.x: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316–1320) abolished the price controls, restored confiscated lands and withdrew the harsh regulations.

new.s: The Mamluk dynasty ruled from Delhi during:
new.x: The Mamluk or Slave dynasty ruled from 1206 to 1290, when the Khaljis took over.

new.s: Who founded the Second Ilbari line of the Mamluk dynasty?
new.x: Balban founded the Second Ilbari line (1266-1290); Iltutmish founded the First Ilbari line and Aibak the Qutbi line.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the lines of the Mamluk dynasty:
1. The Qutbi line was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak.
2. The First Ilbari line was founded by Balban.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Aibak founded the Qutbi line; the First Ilbari line was founded by Iltutmish, while Balban founded the Second Ilbari line.

new.s: Qutbuddin Aibak was a slave of:
new.x: Aibak, sold first to the Qazi of Nishapur, became the slave of Muhammad Ghori (asked in APPSC Group 1, 2004).

new.s: What was the capital of Qutbuddin Aibak?
new.x: Aibak ruled from Lahore; Iltutmish later moved the capital to Delhi.

new.s: The first mosque in Delhi, begun by Qutbuddin Aibak, was:
new.x: Aibak began the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, the first mosque in Delhi; Adhai Din ka Jhonpra is at Ajmer.

new.s: The Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, begun by Qutbuddin Aibak, is located at:
new.x: Aibak began the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer, along with the Qutb Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam in Delhi.

new.s: Which coins did Iltutmish introduce as regular Arabic coinage?
new.x: Iltutmish brought in the silver tanka and the copper jital, a regular, purely Arabic coinage.

new.s: The copper coin of the Delhi Sultanate introduced by Iltutmish was the:
new.x: Iltutmish's coinage had the silver tanka and the copper jital.

new.s: Iltutmish received investiture ('mansur') from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad in:
new.x: In 1229 Iltutmish received the first Caliphal investiture from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad.

new.s: Iltutmish defeated his rival Tajuddin Yildiz at Tarain in:
new.x: Yildiz was defeated at Tarain in 1216; 1192 was the second battle of Tarain under Ghori.

new.s: The Turkan-i-Chahalgani or 'the Forty' created by Iltutmish were:
new.x: The Forty (Chalisa) were a Turkish military elite, not Persian revenue clerks.

new.s: Under Iltutmish, officers who held revenue assignments instead of cash salaries were called:
new.x: Iqtas were revenue assignments given to officers called muqtis in place of cash salaries.

new.s: Razia's favourite Yaqut, resented by the Turkish nobles, was a/an:
new.x: Yaqut was an Abyssinian; the Turkish nobles resented Razia's favour to him.

new.s: Altuniya, who revolted against Razia in 1240, was the governor of:
new.x: Altuniya was governor of Bhatinda (Sirhind); his revolt led to Yaqut's death and Razia's imprisonment.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Razia Sultan:
1. She was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
2. She married Altuniya and was killed after marching on Delhi.
3. She made Balban Diwan-i-Arz.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Razia was the only woman Sultan and married Altuniya before her defeat in 1240; she made Balban Amir-i-Shikar, not Diwan-i-Arz.

new.s: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is named after which Sultan?
new.x: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is named after Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66), whose naib was Balban.

new.s: As naib of Nasiruddin Mahmud, Balban held the title:
new.x: Balban, principal minister and leader of the Forty, bore the title Ulugh Khan.

new.s: Who briefly displaced Balban from power during Nasiruddin Mahmud's reign?
new.x: Imaduddin Raihan briefly displaced Balban, who then returned to power.

new.s: Balban's original name was:
new.x: Balban was born c. 1205 as Bahauddin; captured by the Mongols, he was bought by Iltutmish.

new.s: Which regnal title did Balban take on his accession in 1266?
new.x: Balban took the regnal title Ghiyasuddin Balban in 1266.

new.s: In Balban's court, 'paibos' meant:
new.x: Paibos was kissing the feet; sijda was prostration and zil-i-ilahi meant shadow of God.

new.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched about Balban's court?
new.x: Sijda meant prostration; kissing the feet was paibos.

new.s: Balban separated the military department Diwan-i-Arz from the finance department called:
new.x: Balban's Diwan-i-Arz was separated from the Diwan-i-Wizarat, the finance department.

new.s: Balban's defence against the Mongols relied mainly on:
o: Outposts and forts on the frontier
new.x: Balban built outposts and forts against the Mongols.

new.s: Balban's grandson who succeeded him and was later murdered was:
new.x: Kaiqubad, Balban's grandson, was murdered and his body thrown into the Yamuna; infant Kaimurs followed.

new.s: The last ruler of the Mamluk dynasty was:
new.x: The infant Kaimurs was the last Mamluk before Jalaluddin Khalji crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290.

new.s: What was the reign period of Bahlol Lodi?
new.x: Bahlol Lodi ruled 1451-1489, not 1491.

new.s: The Sayyid Sultan Khizr Khan ruled during:
new.x: Khizr Khan (Sayyid) ruled 1414-1421; he is different from Alauddin's son Khizr Khan, set aside in 1316.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of Sultan and reign is correctly matched?
new.x: Jalaluddin ruled 1290-1296; Alauddin ruled to 1316, Muhammad bin Tughlaq from 1325, and Bahlol Lodi to 1489.

new.s: Jalaluddin Khalji crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290 at about the age of:
new.x: Jalaluddin crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290 aged about 70.

new.s: Which rebel was treated leniently by Jalaluddin Khalji?
new.x: Jalaluddin was lenient to rebels such as Malik Chhajju.

new.s: Jalaluddin Khalji married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, who was a descendant of:
new.x: Jalaluddin married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Chengiz Khan.

new.s: On whose advice did Alauddin Khalji drop his plans of world conquest and a new religion?
new.x: Kotwal of Delhi Ala-ul-Mulk, Barani's uncle, advised him to drop both plans.

new.s: Alauddin Khalji told Qazi Mughisuddin of which place that he acted in the interest of the state?
new.x: Barani records Alauddin's talk with Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana.

new.s: State laws made by the ruler, distinguished by Barani from the Shariat, were called:
new.x: Barani separated Shariat from Zawabit, the state laws made by the ruler.

new.s: Under Jalaluddin Khalji, Alauddin's post of Ariz-i-Mumalik meant:
new.x: Ariz-i-Mumalik was the army minister, not minister of law; Amir-i-Tuzuk was master of ceremonies.

new.s: The court poet of Alauddin Khalji was:
new.x: Amir Khusrau was Alauddin's court poet.

new.s: In which year did Alauddin Khalji conquer Gujarat?
new.x: Gujarat was conquered in 1299 (APPSC 2023 key), not 1297.

new.s: Which Chauhan ruler of Ranthambore was defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1301?
new.x: Hammir Deva Chauhan, who sheltered the New Mussalmans, was defeated at Ranthambore in 1301.

new.s: Which ruler of Malwa was defeated by Alauddin's general Ain-ul-Mulk in 1305?
new.x: Ain-ul-Mulk conquered Malwa from Mahlak Deva in 1305.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alauddin Khalji's conquests?
o: Nusrat Khan was killed at Ranthambore
Chittor was taken from Rana Ratan Singh in 1303
Zafar Khan was killed at Ranthambore
new.x: Nusrat Khan was killed at Ranthambore; Zafar Khan was killed at the Battle of Kili (1299).

new.s: Malik Kafur's campaign of 1310-11 against the Hoysalas of Dwarasamudra was against:
new.x: The Hoysala ruler Vira Ballala III of Dwarasamudra submitted in 1310-11.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Koh-i-Noor and Malik Kafur:
1. A later popular tradition says Kafur obtained it from Prataparudra at Warangal.
2. A contemporary record confirms Kafur obtained it at Warangal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Koh-i-Noor story is only a later popular tradition; there is no contemporary record of it.

new.s: Kakatiya tribute to Delhi under the 1309-10 treaty stopped after:
new.x: After the 1309-10 treaty and help against the Pandyas in 1311, the Kakatiya tribute stopped after 1316.

new.s: Whose troops aided Malik Kafur in his 1311 campaign against Madurai?
new.x: Under the 1309-10 treaty, Kakatiya troops aided Kafur against the Pandyas of Madurai in 1311.

new.s: According to Telugu sources, how many times was Warangal invaded by the Delhi Sultanate?
new.x: Telugu sources count 8 invasions of Warangal; Muslim sources count 5.

new.s: In the Battle of Kili (1299) against the Mongols, which commander of Alauddin was killed?
new.x: Zafar Khan was killed at Kili in 1299; Nusrat Khan was killed at Ranthambore.

new.s: The Mongols in the Battle of Kili (1299) were led by:
new.x: Qutlugh Khwaja led the Mongols at Kili in 1299; Targhi besieged Delhi in 1303.

new.s: The Mongol siege of Delhi in 1303 was led by:
new.x: Targhi besieged Delhi in 1303, and Alauddin sheltered in Siri fort.

new.s: Ghazi Malik is said to have chased away the Mongols how many times?
new.x: By 1320 Ghazi Malik had chased the Mongols 29 times.

new.s: Chittor was conquered by Alauddin Khalji in:
new.x: Alauddin defeated Rana Ratan Singh at Chittor in 1303, after which Padmini and the Rajput women performed jauhar.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Padmini legend:
1. Padmavat was written about two centuries after the Chittor conquest.
2. Rani Padmini and the Rajput women performed jauhar at Chittor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Padmavat (1540) came about two centuries after 1303, and the story says Padmini and the Rajput women performed jauhar.

new.s: After Alauddin's death in 1316, Malik Kafur enthroned which minor prince?
new.x: Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar; Kafur was then murdered.

new.s: Who murdered Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah?
new.x: Khusrau Khan (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah) murdered Mubarak Shah, and was killed by Ghazi Malik in 1320.

new.s: The last Khalji Sultan of Delhi was:
new.x: Mubarak Shah was the last Khalji Sultan; Khusrau Khan was a usurper.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT an aim of Alauddin Khalji's market control?
new.x: The aims were fixed prices, sure supply, rationing and the end of monopolies; it was not meant to pay palace artisans less.

new.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, the Mandi market dealt mainly in:
new.x: The Mandi was the grain market; Sarai Adl dealt in cloth and other goods.

new.s: The whole market system of Alauddin Khalji was run by the:
new.x: The Diwan-i-Riyasat, under the Naib-i-Riyasat, ran the markets; Diwan-i-Mustakhraj recovered revenue arrears.

new.s: How many separate markets did Alauddin Khalji set up?
new.x: There were four markets: Mandi (grain), Sarai Adl (cloth etc.), one for horses, slaves and cattle, and one for miscellaneous goods.

new.s: Malik Kabool under Alauddin Khalji held the post of:
new.x: Malik Kabool was a Shahna-i-Mandi, superintendent of a market.

new.s: The secret spies who sent daily reports to Alauddin Khalji were called:
new.x: Alauddin reorganised spies, the barids and munhiyan, who sent daily reports.

new.s: Which ordinance of Alauddin Khalji was aimed at nobles' intermarriages and gatherings?
o: Royal permission for feasts and marriage alliances
new.x: To check nobles' gatherings and intermarriage, feasts and marriage alliances needed royal permission.

new.s: Alauddin Khalji was the first Sultan to assess land revenue on the basis of:
new.x: Alauddin was the first Sultan to measure land (masahat), with the biswa as the standard unit.

new.s: The standard unit of land measurement under Alauddin Khalji was the:
new.x: Land was measured with the biswa as the standard unit.

new.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, Charai was a tax on:
new.x: Charai was a grazing tax on milch animals; Ghari was the house tax.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue reforms:
1. The privileges of khuts and muqaddams were abolished.
2. Land measurement covered the whole empire.
3. Khalisa land was expanded by reclaiming milk, waqf and inam lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Intermediaries lost their privileges and khalisa grew; measurement was limited to Delhi and nearby areas.

new.s: Which Bahmani minister later copied Alauddin Khalji's dagh and chehra?
new.x: Mahmud Gawan of the Bahmanis brought in dagh, chehra, land measurement and a larger khalisa.

new.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, soldiers of the standing army were paid:
new.x: Alauddin was the first Sultan with a large permanent standing army paid in cash.

new.s: Alauddin Khalji explained to Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana that his acts were guided by:
new.x: He rejected the ulema's advice and told the Qazi he acted in the interest of the state.

new.s: The ruler of Ranthambhore defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1301 was:
new.x: Hammir Deva ruled Ranthambhore (1301); Rai Karan was of Gujarat, Ratan Singh of Chittor and Mahlak Deva of Malwa.

new.s: Which of the following conquest–ruler pairs is wrongly matched?
new.x: Malwa's ruler was Mahlak Deva; Hammir Deva ruled Ranthambhore.

new.s: Malik Kafur's 1310-11 campaign was against the:
new.x: In 1310-11 Kafur marched against the Hoysalas of Dwarasamudra under Vira Ballala III.

new.s: Malik Kafur, called 'Hazar Dinari', rose to the rank of:
new.x: Kafur, a eunuch bought for 1,000 dinars, rose to be Malik Naib (deputy).

new.s: The loot from Warangal in 1309-10 was carried back to Delhi on how many camels?
new.x: Prataparudra submitted and the loot was carried on 1,000 camels.

new.s: Ziauddin Barani's account of Alauddin Khalji's reforms is in:
new.x: Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, the main account of the reforms; Khazain-ul-Futuh is by Amir Khusrau.

new.s: Khazain-ul-Futuh, describing Alauddin Khalji's campaigns, was written by:
new.x: Amir Khusrau, who went on the 1310 campaign, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh.

new.s: Which was the first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
new.x: The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty; they founded Agra.

new.s: Which pair of Delhi Sultanate dynasty and key contribution is wrongly matched?
new.x: Agra was founded by the Lodis; the Tughlaqs are known for token currency, capital transfer and canals.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT an effect of Alauddin Khalji's reforms?
o: An army strong enough to beat the Mongols
Greater freedom and profit for merchants
new.x: Prices stayed stable and the army beat the Mongols, but espionage bred discontent and merchants and peasants were hurt.
